_meta.description: Shell commands and the outcomes Mainwave derives from each. Mainwave's backend rules are the truth: a backend test runs every case through the backend's own SQL. The Mainwave plugin computes the same outcomes on the person's machine and stamps them on the command's tool span, so command text need not leave it, and runs every case through its own implementation from a byte copy of this file. A case changes only by a reviewed edit that changes the backend's rules, never to match one implementation's output.

format.cases: A list of { name, command, outcomes, refs }. `command` is the shell command as the tool ran it, newlines included.
format.outcomes: The counts above 0, by column. A column absent from `outcomes` is 0. The plugin sends each one as the integer attribute `mainwave.command.<column>` on the command's `claude_code.tool` span, and sends none that is 0.
format.refs: The refs the command names, by name, each the pattern's raw capture (not normalized: `HEAD:refs/heads/x` stays as written). A ref absent from `refs` is none. Each rides beside its count: `branch_opened` with `branches_opened`, `push_ref` with `pushes`, `merge_ref` with `merges`, `tag_name` with `tags`. The plugin sends each as the string attribute `mainwave.command.<name>`, only while the `repo` data point is on.
format.counted: The presence key: the plugin sends the integer attribute `mainwave.command.counted` (1) on every shell command's `claude_code.tool` span, succeeded or not, while the `bash.outcome` data point is on, with or without counts. A span with it has known outcomes, so a command that made none reads as 0, not as a command whose outcomes weren't captured. Not a case field.

columns.commits: `git commit` and `git cherry-pick` at a command position (the outcome counts' commits). `git revert` is not one.
columns.reverts: `git revert`. The Activity rollup's commit count is `commits` plus `reverts`.
columns.prs_updated: `gh pr edit|ready|comment|review`, `gh stack submit|push`, `glab mr update|note|approve`.
columns.merges: `git merge` invocations that are not a branch sync (a `--ff-only` merge of a remote-tracking ref or of none).
columns.tags: `git tag <name>` (not listing or deleting) and `gh|glab release create`.
columns.branches_opened: 1 when the command opens a branch (`git checkout -b|-B`, `git switch -c|-C|--create|--force-create`, `git worktree add -b|-B`), however many it opens. A flag, not a count.

ref_names.branch_opened: The branch the first branch open names.
ref_names.push_ref: The ref the first `git push <remote> <ref>` names; a push with no ref names none.
ref_names.merge_ref: The ref the last `git merge` that is not a sync names.
ref_names.tag_name: The tag the first `git tag` names; a CLI release names none.

_meta.rules: A command position is the start of the command or a point after `&&`, `;`, `|` or a newline, past `rtk`, `do`, `then`, `else`, `if`, `until` or `while`. Heredoc bodies, quoted strings holding a separator or a newline, and comments are cut before matching, so text there never counts. `git -C <dir>` may precede a subcommand.
_meta.scope: The plugin stamps counts and refs only on a shell command that succeeded, and `counted` on every shell command; command text, when collected, counts every command run. A span with command text is counted from it and never from stamps.
